title: Read exact PR, Issue and commit bodies through shared transports
body:
## Purpose
Make selected GitHub content accessible without treating compact PR identity or search previews as full content. Implements a focused part of #20; leaves the local Git migration in #23 independent.

## Changes
- content(repo, kind, identifier) reads exact PR/Issue descriptions or the complete commit message through existing gh/urllib and cumulative operation limits.
- Validate repository, number/kind or full commit SHA and canonical web URL. Preserve null vs empty descriptions and Unicode/newlines; missing/malformed body/message fails closed.
- content_from_hit re-reads selected search/discovery identity. select_content projects explicit fields offline while preserving identity/provenance.
- Add content CLI with repeatable --field. Existing pr(), issue(), search and digest contracts remain compatible.
- Explain clone/shallow history vs GitHub records and current diff/blame ownership. No new transport/parser/dependency/write operation.

## Validation
251 passed, 95 subtests passed across the full suite; JUnit generated. Compile and content CLI help pass; git diff --check clean. 29 new test cases cover three kinds, gh/urllib normalization, search-to-body handoff, offline selection, wrong identities, missing/null/empty content, Unicode, invalid selectors, byte-limit propagation and CLI errors. Actual public API responses for this repo PR #23, Issue #20 and main commit 8dc232c... were retrieved through the GitHub connector and passed through the parser locally; this is payload validation, not live execution of GHI's own transport. Published tree matches tested index 68e7513ea845f2aab5900e0dad719d0b39ea051e.

## Remaining boundaries
Descriptions are not conversation comments or review bodies. Commit body is the complete message including subject, not a patch. Commit search, remote file/diff pagination, comparison and full comment/review selection remain #20 work; #23 owns existing local git diff/show/log/blame. No automatic clone/fetch or partial-history completeness claim. No merge performed.
